validity.recommendation: Real, well-documented shelved proposal — no existence/duplicate/classification problem. Two housekeeping fixes: (1) swap the Status [ref] citation off PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 (which only documents the pending 2020 EoI, not the 2022 shelving) onto the Petrowatch Feb-2022 article, which is the actual source for 'shelved'; (2) note but do NOT act on gem.wiki's own unverifiable Dec-2022 IGX-map claim (link now 404) that would suggest the project was still 'under development' after the drop — treat it as an open flag, not evidence against shelved.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE — all clear. This is a genuine, extensively paper-trailed GSPL proposal, not a phantom entity: EIA/TOR filed May 2016 (environmentclearance.nic.in TOR doc, currently 503 — Indian govt server flakiness, not evidence of deletion, could not re-verify this session); a Mar-2018 project listing at project cost INR 1,058.40 cr (projectstiger.com, verified live, existence + cost only); a detailed Nov-2019 project-tracker writeup (indianpetroplus.com, verified live) describing it as a 'greenfield' Anjar(Kachchh)-Chotila(Surendranagar) line, 196.14 km, 36-inch diameter, 23.13 MMSCMD design capacity, 8+1 SV/IP stations, EIA consultant AnaconLabs, cost 1,058 cr, with authorization pending after GSPL's 2012 authorization on the corridor lapsed; a formal Jan-2020 EoI to PNGRB revised the headline figure to 'minimum 13 MMSCMD including common carrier capacity' (per GAIL's official 30-Jun-2020 comment letter to PNGRB, pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/GAIL01072020.pdf — url_verifier FAILs the substring screen on this one but pdftotext -layout confirms the PDF literally contains 'Anjar Chotila Natural Gas Pipeline', GSPL, and the 13 MMSCMD figure; a known verifier false-negative per its own docstring, not a dead/wrong link); the PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 (p.40, sourced ref) restates the same Jan-2020 EoI as 'under process' at 200 km / 13 MMSCMD / Gujarat State Petronet. GAIL's letter also clarifies the CLASSIFICATION context: there is already an EXISTING GSPL pipeline along the Mundra-Anjar-Chotila corridor (part of GSPL's High-Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid, authorised 2012), and the EoI project is explicitly described as a parallel 'loop line' / capacity-expansion filing under PNGRB Regulation 12 — i.e., new physical pipe built alongside the existing corridor, not a relabeling of the existing asset. That existing 2012 corridor is not among this batch's 27-item roster and is out of scope; P0905 correctly represents only the standalone loop proposal, so this is NOT a duplicate of anything in-scope. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both already ref-supported (existing_ref_checks ok:true) and correct — a loop line off a high-pressure transmission grid is still transmission-class, not gathering/feeder. STATUS: the sheet's 'shelved' is independently confirmed by 'Frustrated GSPL drops Anjar-Chotila pipeline' (Petrowatch, Vol 25 PW 5, 10-Feb-2022, verified live) — 'Almost six years after proposing it, Gujarat State Petronet (GSPL) has finally [dropped it]' (full text paywalled beyond the lede, but headline+dek is unambiguous and dated). This closes the loop on a clean timeline: proposed 2016 -> EIA 2016/2018 listing -> Jan-2020 fresh EoI (13 MMSCMD) -> expected commissioning Dec-2021 per an 8-Jun-2021 Financial Express/Edelweiss analyst note on GSPL ('the Anjar-Chotila pipeline should be commissioned by Dec 2021, which is likely to augment incremental ~5mmscmd volumes from CY22', verified live) -> formally dropped, Feb-2022 (Petrowatch). The current live PNGRB register (May-2026 edition, pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, verified 200/genuine via manual pdftotext) still carries NO Anjar-Chotila / GSPL entry in Operational, Partially Commissioned, or Under Construction — consistent with 'never authorised, dropped' four years on. CAVEAT #1 (ref-quality defect, not a value defect): the sheet's existing Status [ref] cites PNGRB AR2019-20, which is a genuinely dead end for this purpose — its own existing_ref_checks entry already flags 'value not found (none of [shelved])', and reading it confirms why: as of that 2020 report the EoI was merely 'under process', months before commissioning was even expected. The AR2019-20 doc is a fine ref for Length/Capacity/Owner/Route (see fills) but does not and cannot support Status=shelved. Recommend swapping the Status [ref] to the Petrowatch article. CAVEAT #2 (open flag, not actioned): gem.wiki's own article (read for leads only, never cited) asserts a further wrinkle — a citation to an IGX (Indian Gas Exchange) infrastructure map dated 30-Dec-2022 allegedly showing the pipeline as 'under development', i.e. AFTER Petrowatch's Feb-2022 'dropped' report. I could not verify this independently: the URL (igxindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/NGInfrastructure_30_Dec22.pdf) 404s and no Wayback capture was reachable this session (archive.org rate-limited every attempt). Since (a) the claim is unverifiable, (b) it has only one weak backlink on the wiki page, and (c) the far more recent and authoritative May-2026 PNGRB register still shows zero authorisation, I do NOT recommend changing Status off 'shelved' on the strength of this dangling citation — but it is worth a human spot-check if the IGX PDF ever becomes reachable again, since a gas-exchange infrastructure map published 10 months after the 'drop' story would be a real tension if confirmed. SPEC note: an earlier (Nov-2019, pre-EoI) concept design quoted 23.13 MMSCMD and 196.14 km/36in; the Jan-2020 EoI actually filed with PNGRB (and reported in the AR2019-20 + GAIL's letter, both 2020) cites 'minimum 13 MMSCMD' and the sheet's 200 km is a reasonable round of the 196.14 km design figure — read as: capacity was scaled down between the 2019 concept and the 2020 filing, and the LATER, filed number (13 MMSCMD) is correctly the one currently on the sheet. Not a live disagreement to flag.

fills.researcher_notes: Replacement, not addition: current Status [ref] (PNGRB AR2019-20) does not support 'shelved' (confirmed by its own existing_ref_checks flag and by reading it — it only documents the pending 2020 EoI). This Petrowatch article ('Frustrated GSPL drops Anjar-Chotila pipeline', 10-Feb-2022) is the actual source for the shelving and is independently corroborated by the current (May-2026) PNGRB NGPL register showing zero live authorisation for this line.

PNGRB AR2019-20 p.40 gives the route Anjar-Bhachau-Maliya-Thangadh-Chotila at exactly 'Length: 200 km' (matches the sheet exactly; pdftotext-confirmed, the automated substring screen already passes on this doc for other fields). IndianPetroPlus (Nov-2019, independent project-tracker, pre-dates and is editorially separate from the EoI/PNGRB paper trail) gives the more granular original design figure of 196.14 km — the sheet's 200 is a reasonable round of that same physical route, not a conflicting value.

PNGRB AR2019-20 p.40 gives 'Capacity: 13 MMSCMD' verbatim (matches sheet exactly). GAIL's 30-Jun-2020 comment letter to PNGRB independently states 'total minimum capacity of the proposed pipeline has been mentioned as 13 MMSCMD including common carrier capacity' (pdftotext-confirmed; the automated url_verifier substring screen FAILs on this PDF — false negative, verified manually, see docstring on large/PDF-extraction false negatives). Marked tier=medium/independent=false rather than high, because both documents are ultimately reporting the same underlying Jan-2020 GSPL EoI filing rather than two separately-derived measurements — a regulator's report and a third party's official comment on the SAME filing, not two origins. An earlier (Nov-2019, pre-EoI) concept design had quoted 23.13 MMSCMD (indianpetroplus.com) — noted in validity notes as a superseded design figure, not cited here since it disagrees with the value being sourced.

PNGRB AR2019-20 route: 'Anjar-Bhachau-Maliya-Thangadh-Chotila'. GAIL's letter independently names the 'Mundra-Anjar-Chotila route' / 'Anjar-Chotila pipeline' (pdftotext-confirmed; verifier false negative on this PDF, see Capacity fill note). Both agree on Anjar (Kachchh)/Chotila (Surendranagar), Gujarat, India — matches sheet. Minor wrinkle for the record, not actioned: indianpetroplus.com's 2019 writeup describes the pipeline as 'originating' near Ratanpar village in Surendranagar (Chotila side) and 'terminating' at a GSPL station near Rata Talav in Kutch (Anjar side) — i.e. construction/engineering origin-terminus wording runs opposite to the Anjar->Chotila naming convention. This looks like a construction-direction vs. naming-convention artifact rather than a real endpoint dispute (every other source, including the two cited here, uses Anjar-first naming), so it is not treated as a location conflict.

PNGRB AR2019-20 names 'Gujarat State Petronet Limited' as the sponsoring entity for the Jan-2020 EoI. IndianPetroPlus (Nov-2019, editorially separate/earlier) independently states 'Gujarat State Petronet Limited (GSPL) is planning to construct the Anjar (Kachchh)-Chotila (Surendranagar) Natural Gas transportation pipeline'. Sole-owner 100% is consistent across every source found; no co-developer ever named.

Diameter was genuinely blank. Single source found: IndianPetroPlus (Nov-2019) gives 'with a dia of 36 inch' for the as-designed greenfield line. Could not corroborate with a second independent source this session — the environmentclearance.nic.in TOR/EIA filing that likely also states diameter returned HTTP 503 on every retry (Indian govt server flakiness, not a dead/removed page), and a Scribd mirror of the GSPL EIA (scribd.com/document/563293745) is paywalled behind a login and returned no extractable text. Staged as medium/single-source per standing rule 4 rather than withheld, since a sourced diameter is flagged as high-value for this country and the figure is internally consistent (36in is a plausible diameter for a 13-23 MMSCMD, 200km transmission loop). Flag for a second source if the TOR PDF becomes reachable again.

Upgrading DelayType from the current blank/'inferred' to 'confirmed': the delay is explicitly source-documented, not a dormancy-rule inference. An 8-Jun-2021 Financial Express/Edelweiss analyst note on GSPL states 'the Anjar-Chotila pipeline should be commissioned by Dec 2021' as a live near-term expectation; the Petrowatch article (10-Feb-2022) confirms that target was missed and GSPL 'finally' dropped the project instead — a sourced miss of a sourced target, six years after proposing it in 2016.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Direct dated evidence: Petrowatch, 'Frustrated GSPL drops Anjar-Chotila pipeline' (Vol 25 PW 5, 10-Feb-2022) — GSPL formally dropped the project six years after proposing it, matching the sheet's 'shelved'. This is not a PNGRB authorisation dating trap: the AR2019-20 EoI process never converted into an authorisation, so there is no 'authorisation date vs commissioning date' confusion here — the project simply never got authorised. Most-recent corroborating evidence: the current live PNGRB NGPL MIS register (May-2026 edition, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, verified genuine via manual pdftotext after the automated substring screen false-negatived on 'Petroleum' — a known large-PDF extraction gap) still carries ZERO entry for Anjar-Chotila/GSPL in any of Operational / Partially Commissioned / Under Construction, four years after the drop — i.e. it was never re-authorised. One unresolved wrinkle, NOT acted on: gem.wiki's own article (read for leads only) cites an unreachable igxindia.com infrastructure-map PDF dated 30-Dec-2022 that it says showed the line as 'under development' — ten months after the Petrowatch drop story. I could not independently verify this (404, and Wayback lookups were rate-limited every attempt this session); given it is a single, now-dead citation against two live independent confirmations (the drop story + the current register's continued absence), I am not treating it as grounds for a status change, but it is worth a human recheck if that PDF or a Wayback capture ever becomes reachable. Sheet's ShelvedCancelledType is not currently populated on this row per the worklist units seen; if set, 'confirmed' (not 'inferred') is the correct value given the Petrowatch sourcing — but that column was not surfaced as a unit for this row so no fill was staged for it here.

summary: P0905 Anjar-Chotila Gas Pipeline: verdict confirmed (caveat), concern_type none — real GSPL loop-line proposal (2016-2022), correctly shelved per an independently-verified Feb-2022 Petrowatch report and continued absence from the live May-2026 PNGRB register; staged 7 fills (Status-ref swap off a non-supporting citation, Length/Capacity/Location/Owner ref-ins, a new sourced Diameter=36in, and Delayed/DelayType upgrade to confirmed) plus a status_reviews confirm. No existence, duplicate, or classification problems found. UNRESOLVED: a single dangling gem.wiki citation (Dec-2022 IGX map, link dead) claiming the project looked 'under development' after it was reportedly dropped — flagged as an open watch item, not actioned, since it is unverifiable and outweighed by two live independent confirmations of shelved.
